correctness.rationale: The negative-t Chebyshev parametrization converts the nonnegativity requirement exactly into a one-dimensional maximum, proving both sufficiency and necessity of the stated floor. The maximizer equation and uniqueness follow from monotone logarithmic-derivative terms. The finite-n and asymptotic constants follow from convexity, elementary maximization, and uniform convergence. Replacing only the additive floor leaves the source proof's polynomial degrees unchanged, so the refined floor propagates through the same quadratic-module argument.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2026 source introduces the Chebyshev desingularization but uses a multiplicity-independent floor obtained by discarding the factor 1-V_n^{d-1}. It does not state the exact multiplicity-sensitive minimum floor, its worst-multiplicity envelope, the beta_d/kappa_d constants, or the resulting refinement of its theorem constant. Searches of exact and synonymous formulations found no prior coverage. Earlier univariate quadratic-module and exact Stengle literature addresses different structural or problem-specific questions. Originality is only to the best of our knowledge.

value.rationale: The result converts the source's qualitative statement that boundary degeneracy affects constants into an explicit sharp multiplicity law for the central Chebyshev recovery primitive. It gives strict finite-n improvements at every fixed odd multiplicity without increasing certificate degree, and it quantifies the reduction substantially for cubic and other low multiplicities.
